title: Attorney Estate Administration Workflow Guide (August 2026)
summary: Estate administration workflow for attorneys covering intake, inventory, creditor claims, and tax filing deadlines. August 2026.
body_markdown:
Estate administration covers the legal and administrative steps required to wind down a decedent's affairs, satisfy creditors, and transfer assets to distributees or beneficiaries. This guide covers key points for attorneys to know about the estate administration process.


**Key Takeaways**


- Letters Testamentary must be in hand before any account access or property transfer can occur.
- Creditor claims periods range from 3 months (Florida) to 7 months (New York); distributing assets before they close can expose the personal representative to personal liability.
- Form 4768 extends the filing deadline for estate tax, not the payment deadline; tax owed is still due at the 9-month mark.
- Elayne organizes intake and runs asset discovery across 100+ financial sources, with intake completing in an average of 2 days and billed per matter as an eligible estate expense.


## What Estate Administration Covers


In the context of estate administration, an attorney's engagement covers the legal and administrative steps required to wind down a decedent's affairs, satisfy creditors, and transfer assets to the rightful distributees or beneficiaries.


Testate estates move through probate with a valid will; intestate estates proceed under state succession statutes, often with added court supervision and longer timelines. Trust administration runs on a separate track entirely, governed by the trust instrument instead of the probate court.


[Estate administration process](https://www.elayne.com/resources/what-is-estate-administration) determines which assets pass through the court proceeding and require Letters Testamentary or letters of administration before any transfer occurs.[Non-probate assets](https://www.elayne.com/resources/probate-vs-non-probate-assets) , including beneficiary-designated accounts, jointly held property, and trust assets, transfer by operation of law and sit outside the court proceeding.

## Matter Intake and Opening the Estate


Intake begins before court filings. Attorneys need, at minimum, the original will (if testate), certified copies of[the death certificate](https://www.usa.gov/death-certificate) , and enough information about the decedent's domicile to confirm the correct jurisdiction. Where the decedent was domiciled at death determines which court hears the proceeding, which forms apply, and which notice statutes govern.


Once the proceeding type is confirmed, the petition for probate or administration goes to the appropriate court. Requirements vary by state and by county. New York Surrogate's Court practice, for instance, differs county to county in terms of local forms, clerk expectations, and scheduling norms.


A complete intake packet from the personal representative should include:


- Certified death certificate copies, since institutions typically require originals or certified copies instead of photocopies
- The original will and any codicils
- The decedent's full legal name, date of birth, domicile location, and Social Security number
- A preliminary asset list identifying probate versus non-probate property
- Names, mailing details, and relationships of all distributees and named beneficiaries


[Letters Testamentary](https://www.elayne.com/resources/what-are-letters-testamentary) or letters of administration issue once the court approves the petition.


## Government Agency Notifications After Death


Notifying the Social Security Administration and the IRS are separate obligations, and neither substitutes for the other.


SSA notification typically flows through the funeral home, which reports the death. Otherwise, the personal representative contacts SSA directly. IRS notification runs on a different track and requires three steps:


- Form 56 (Notice Concerning Fiduciary Relationship) to confirm the personal representative's authority with the IRS
- Form 8822 to update the decedent's mailing location of record if needed
- An[EIN for the estate account](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-get-ein-number-for-estate-account) , required before opening an estate bank account or filing Form 1041


## Building the Estate Inventory and the Diligent Search Obligation


The[probate estate inventory](https://www.elayne.com/resources/how-to-list-assets-and-debts-for-the-court-during-probate) is the personal representative's formal accounting of all probate assets at date-of-death values. The attorney's role is to guide that process and make sure the fiduciary's diligent-search obligation is met.


Asset categories for the inventory include:


- Real property and recorded deeds
- Financial accounts, brokerage accounts, and retirement accounts
- Life insurance policies with the estate as beneficiary
- Unclaimed and state-held property
- Business interests, partnership interests, and closely held stock
- Digital assets and online accounts with monetary value


Date-of-death valuation applies to every probate asset. Account values use the date-of-death balance; real property requires a qualified appraisal. Retirement accounts with named beneficiaries fall outside the probate estate but still need to be identified and documented so SECURE Act 2.0 distribution obligations surface correctly.


## Notice to Creditors: Requirements and State Deadlines


[Notice to creditors](https://www.elayne.com/resources/notice-to-creditors-requirements) runs on two parallel tracks: published notice to unknown creditors and direct written notice to known creditors. Both are required in most states, and neither satisfies the other.


Publication must appear in a court-approved newspaper in the county of administration. Once published, the personal representative files an affidavit of publication with the court to confirm compliance. The claims period does not begin until publication runs.


Examples from different states:


State Creditor Claims Period


Florida 3 months after first publication


California 4 months after Letters issue


Illinois 6 months after Letters issue


New York 7-month fiduciary liability window


A personal representative who distributes assets before the claims period closes risks personal liability for any valid creditor claim that surfaces afterward. That exposure is individual and reaches beyond estate funds. Defective notice, whether from wrong publication, a missed direct notice to a known creditor, or a filing error, can extend the claims period or void distributions entirely. The exact consequence depends on state law.

## Tax Filing Obligations and Key Deadlines


Return Obligation Due Date


Form 1040 Final personal return; income Jan 1 through date of death April 15 of the year following death


Form 1041 Estate income; required when gross income reaches $600 after death; filed each year the estate remains open; fiscal year election available April 15 for calendar-year estates. For fiscal-year estates, the due date is the 15th day of the fourth month after the fiscal year ends.


Form 706 Federal estate tax; required for gross estates exceeding the[$15 million federal exclusion](https://www.elayne.com/resources/federal-estate-tax-exemption-what-it-means) for 2026 decedents 9 months after date of death; 6-month extension via Form 4768

## FAQs


### What are some of the key tax deadlines an executor should be aware of?


The final Form 1040 is due April 15 of the year following death; Form 1041 (estate income) is due April 15 for calendar-year estates or the 15th day of the fourth month after a fiscal year closes; and Form 706 (federal estate tax, required when the gross estate exceeds $15 million in 2026) is due nine months after the date of death, with a six-month filing extension available via Form 4768. Filing extensions do not extend the payment deadline.


### How do I notify Social Security and the IRS after a family member dies?


See the Government Agency Notifications section above.


### What does an attorney need at intake to open an estate matter?


At minimum: the original will (if testate), certified death certificate copies, the decedent's full legal name, date of birth, domicile location, and Social Security number, a preliminary list of probate versus non-probate assets, and names and mailing details of all distributees and named beneficiaries. The domicile location determines which court hears the proceeding, which forms apply, and which notice statutes govern. Letters Testamentary cannot issue until the petition is complete.


### How does Elayne helps executors and family members collaborate on settling an estate together?


Elayne provides a shared dashboard where authorized family members, co-executors, and attorneys can access documents, track progress, and coordinate steps in one place with role-based permissions. For dual-role executors serving as both executor and beneficiary, the shared dashboard also functions as an auditable record of actions taken, helping show impartial fiduciary administration if any beneficiary later disputes the process.
